title: Like a log
hookLine: the car comes back on empty again, and the words are already in your mouth; Shantideva says: stay like a log
carry: when anger wants to speak, stay like wood
tomorrow: how early can you catch it? before the first step?

lines: THE GAS LIGHT IS ON. AGAIN.
cards: Your sister borrowed the car again. You hear the door, and the keys hit the counter, and you already know. The gas light is on.
Again. She walks into the kitchen humming, and the sentence is ready in your mouth, sharp and perfectly built. You've rehearsed it twice.
Your shoulders are up near your ears. Your hand is already pointing. One breath from now, it's going to come out.
And right there, in that half second, Shantideva has a very strange piece of advice.

teach.b: When you see that your mind is grabbing or wants to strike out, he tells the bodhisattva in training, don't act and don't speak. Stay like a log: kashtha, a piece of wood. Then he widens it.
When the mind wants to mock someone, or boast, or pick at another person's faults, or fish for praise: stay like a log.
The picture is almost funny on purpose. Wood doesn't argue. Wood doesn't type.

teach.h: NOT FOREVER, JUST WHILE IT BURNS.
teach.b: Wood just lies there while the moment passes over it. And here's what makes it more than holding your breath. The log isn't forever.
It's for the stretch while the mind is on fire. Shantideva isn't saying the gas tank doesn't matter, or that you never speak. He's saying don't let anger hold the pen.
Stay still until the heat drops, then talk about the car. So back to the kitchen. The sentence is ready.
Instead of firing it, you set both hands flat on the counter, and you stay there, wooden, for three slow breaths.
She's still humming. The sentence is still there. But now you get to choose which version of it to say.

how: Tibetan teachers in particular often cite Shantideva's 'remain like a log' as a practical instruction: when a strong emotion takes hold, pause speech and action until the mind settles, then respond.

o: falling into a deep, heavy sleep after hard work
being still as wood until anger or pride passes
staying stubborn and refusing to change your mind

games.q: the log, step by step — tap the pairs.
p: a mind that wants to strike out
stay like a log for these too
just while the mind is on fire

s: staying like a log means you never speak up about what's wrong
it's for the stretch while anger burns; then you talk about the car.
Shantideva says to stay like a log when you want to boast or mock, not only when angry
he lists mocking, boasting, picking at faults and fishing for praise.
the log verse is instruction for how to sit in meditation
it's for daily life: the moment a grabbing or angry mind wants to act or speak.

games.q: in a group project meeting, a teammate takes credit for your slide. your face goes hot and you're about to cut in. what's the log move?
o: cut in right away, before the moment passes and nobody remembers.
stay still and quiet till the heat drops, then raise it calmly.
say nothing at all, ever, so the team stays peaceful.
games.why: the log is for while the mind is on fire, not forever. once the heat drops, you can still say what's true.

practice: Settle into one posture and decide not to adjust it until the sit ends. When an urge to move comes, an itch, a shift, a fidget, notice it and stay put, like a log. Watch the urge rise, peak and fade while your body keeps still.

wordCard.voice: Like a log: Shantideva's advice for the moment anger or pride wants to speak. Be still as wood until it passes.

orig.note: Sanskrit: wood, a log or piece of timber. Shantideva: remain like wood.

carryVoice: Hold this one: when anger wants to speak, stay like wood, just until the heat drops, and then say what's true. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 5.48-5.54 (when the mind is attached or wishes to be angry, do not act or speak but remain like a log; likewise when it is proud, mocking, fault-finding, deceitful, or seeking praise)
